canonicalText: Civic Hall announced a January 30, 2016, 1-3 p.m. New York City Council hackathon focused on constituent services.

publicVariants.callnyc-case-study: On January 30, 2016, Civic Hall hosted a New York City Council hackathon focused on constituent services; Civic Hall advertised a 1-3 p.m. workshop window.

evidence.note: Directly supports the announced date, time window, Council connection, and constituent-services purpose.
Preserves the announcement inside an embedded social feed.

qualifier: The 1-3 p.m. value is the advertised workshop window, not proof that every activity occurred for exactly those hours.
limitations: No full agenda or complete event schedule has been recovered.
antiClaims: The 1-3 p.m. announcement proves every activity occurred for exactly those hours.
reviewedBy: Jamie Burkart with AI-assisted archival review

canonicalText: A New York City Council event-day post identified the Civic Hall gathering as its first CouncilStat hackathon.
qualifier: 'First CouncilStat hackathon' is the Council's description, not a broader claim about all civic-data hackathons.
limitations: The Wayback page preserves the post inside an embedded feed; it is not a dedicated event listing.
antiClaims: This was the New York City Council's first civic-data hackathon.
The Wayback capture is a recovered event page or calendar listing.

canonicalText: Jamie's participant archive documents a breakout prompt reading 'Digital District - Help improve City Council District office operations' at approximately 2:10 p.m. on January 30, 2016.

qualifier: Approximately 2:10 p.m. is the photograph timestamp, not an event start time.
limitations: The photograph does not identify every person, role, organizer, facilitator, or collaborator shown.
antiClaims: Digital District was the official title of the full event.

canonicalText: Council offices used CouncilStat differently and with different frequency, so case counts could not responsibly be treated as a simple measure of office performance, specialization, or resident need.

evidence.note: Politico reported staff cautions that offices used CouncilStat in different ways and with different frequency.

qualifier: The public interpretation adds the responsible limit that raw counts should not be treated as simple comparative scores.
limitations: The article does not provide a complete office-by-office data-quality audit.
antiClaims: CouncilStat counts measured office performance, quality, specialization, or need.
The Council adopted a specific participant recommendation unless a source says so.
